---
title: The truth manifest
guide-section: "Generating studies"
---

Real studies don't come with an answer key. Synthetic ones can: `Study.truth` records what a study
was built to show and what its generated data actually shows, so you can check an analysis program
against known values.

## Targets and realised values

For a parallel-group study, the manifest has the target mean change from baseline in each arm, and
the mean change the study's ADaM realised at the end of treatment:

```{python}
import trialforge as tf

trial = tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=300, seed=1, indication="hypertension", weeks=12)
trial.truth["endpoint"]
```

The realised values are computed from the generated ADaM datasets, so an analysis that reproduces
them reads the data correctly. They differ from the targets by sampling error, as a real study's
estimates differ from the true effect. The manifest also records the request itself (archetype,
seed, controls) and other realised quantities, such as treatment-emergent AE incidence:

```{python}
list(trial.truth)
```

## Calibrated targets

Where a control is a clinical target, trialforge solves for the latent model parameters that give
it. In the oncology archetypes, overall survival and progression follow Weibull proportional
hazards models linked by a Gaussian copula, and tumour courses follow RECIST 1.1. The medians and
hazard ratios have exact solutions; confirmed response rates (which depend on the assessment
schedule and the confirmation rule) are calibrated by simulation on a fixed 40,000-subject cohort.

```{python}
onc = tf.study("oncology_solid_tumor", n=400, seed=1, os_hr=0.7, orr=[0.4, 0.2])
onc.truth["targets"]
```

The realised values are what a standard analysis of this study's ADaM gives: Kaplan-Meier medians
and a stratified Cox hazard ratio with its 95% confidence interval.

```{python}
onc.truth["overall_survival"]
```

```{python}
onc.truth["confirmed_orr"]
```

`truth["calibration"]` reports the response rates the calibrated model gives on the calibration
cohort, and whether every target was reachable. A rate above what the assessment schedule allows
(when too many subjects progress or die before a response can be confirmed, say) is clamped to the
highest reachable one:

```{python}
onc.truth["calibration"]
```

## Interim cuts

An interim cut of an event-driven study reports its cutoff date and how many subjects had been
randomised by then:

```{python}
tf.study("oncology_solid_tumor", n=400, seed=1, interim_months=12).truth["interim"]
```

## In files

`Study.write()` and `Study.write_submission()` write the manifest as `truth.json` next to the
datasets.
